newsitem.title: USA: Stocks up on weak data, bargain hunting.
newsitem.headline: Stocks up on weak data, bargain hunting.

text.p: Stocks rose Thursday on fresh signs that inflation was in check and as investors snapped up bargains after a wave of profit-taking.

At 1 p.m. EDT, the Dow Jones indudstrial average was up 18.12 to 5,895.48. In the broader market, advancing issues led declines by 13-to-8 on moderate volume of 299 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.

Major stock indices were higher at the opening bell after the release of August durable goods orders and weekly jobless claims that pointed to tame inflation, sending the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond soaring.
The 30-year bond rose 19/32 to yield 6.88 percent, down from 6.93 percent at Wednesday's close.

Some investors, jittery about upcoming third quarter earnings reports, seized the chance to take profits, sending the broader market lower, analysts said. Later, stocks erased the losses, fuelled by a rally in technology stocks.
"Money managers really want to show an investment in tech stocks on the books as the end of the quarter nears," said Robert von Pentz, a managing partner at Columbia Partners.
Lehman Brothers chief investment strategist Jeffrey Applegate said upcoming third quarter earnings were weighing on the market, adding to its fluctuations.

"We've had some big bad news from AT&T Corp., Dial Corp. and Silicon Graphics Inc., and the market is struggling with it. But I don't think there's any information content yet that suggests were going to have a bad quarter," Applegate said.
He said in the prior quarter, a few companies had set off warning bells for many investors with early profit warnings, but that earnings had modestly exceed expectations in the end.

Gains in DuPont Co. and Merck & Co. Inc. boosted the Dow. Merck added 1-5/8 to 70-3/8. DuPont climbed 1-3/8 to 88-1/2 after it forecast strong quarterly earnings, lifted by its upstream petroleum operations.

Transportation stocks continued to weigh on the market, with the Dow Jones Transport Index 11.41 points lower at 2,060.19 as energy prices and concerns about the domestic economy dragged down the sector's prospects.
"Consumer cyclicals and transportation stocks have been among the worst performing sectors because they are both cyclical and domestic," Applegate said.

"If the Fed were to tighten (raise interest rates), slowing gross domestic product, they would have the most to lose. Or, if the Fed does not have to tighten because the economy is slowing, they still are the most at risk," he said.

Shares in Abercrombie & Fitch Co. surged nearly 40 percent after its initial public offering. Shares of the retailer which outfitted safaris for Theodore Roosevelt and Ernest Hemingway, climbed 6-1/4 to 22-1/4 from their initial price of $16 a share.
Transport Holdings shares jumped 17-3/4 to 69-1/2 after Conseco Inc. bid $70 a share in stock for Transport.
The Nasdaq composite index rose 11.62 points to 1,236.28, and the American Stock Exchange index rose 1.66 to 567.55.
